title: Identification of scalar projection squares through completion
statement:
Fix the finite-field datum of [def-pur-conventions], with algebraic closure $k$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and finite extensions $E\subset F$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Write $A=\mathcal O_E$, $B=\mathcal O_F$, $t=\varpi_E$, $v=\varpi_F$ and $e\geq1$ with $tB=v^eB$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, and fix a compactification $c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p_c}Y)$ with $j$ open and $p_c$ proper [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties, def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,W}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients] and $C_W=-\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. Let $M\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\mathcal O_E)$, the derived-complete bounded constructible category with a uniform Tor-amplitude interval for all reductions [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Write $A_n=A/t^n$, $B_n=B/t^nB=B/v^{en}$, $M_n=M\otimes^L_{R_X}(A_n)_X$, and $C_W^{(n)}=-\otimes^L_{(A_n)_W}(B_n)_W$. For $H=E,F$, let $P_H^c$ be the integral compact-support functor attached to $c$, defined as the total derived inverse limit of its finite separately derived proper/open images [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support]. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\mathcal O_E)$. Use the completed integral pullback and completed tensor [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Let $\gamma_N:C_YP_E^cN\to P_F^cC_XN$ be the map $r_e^{-1}\mathsf R(q_\bullet^c)\tau$ defined by the strict scalar mate and the normalized limit construction [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate, lem-pur-compact-support-scalar-limit-reduction]. Let $\operatorname{PF}_H^c$ denote the actual counit-defined proper/open compact-support projection transformation for $H=E,F$ [def-exchange-projection]. Then the following two composites agree, under the canonical scalar tensor and scalar pullback identifications:
$$
C_Y(P_E^cM\widehat\otimes K)
\xrightarrow{C_Y\operatorname{PF}_E^c}
C_YP_E^c(M\widehat\otimes f_E^*K)
\xrightarrow{\gamma_{M\widehat\otimes f_E^*K}}
P_F^cC_X(M\widehat\otimes f_E^*K)
$$
and
$$
C_Y(P_E^cM\widehat\otimes K)\cong C_YP_E^cM\widehat\otimes C_YK
\xrightarrow{\gamma_M\widehat\otimes1}P_F^cC_XM\widehat\otimes C_YK
\xrightarrow{\operatorname{PF}_F^c}P_F^c(C_XM\widehat\otimes f_F^*C_YK).
$$
Their equality already holds for the finite quotient projection maps on the ringed diagram sites. At integral coefficients, under the canonical direct-image/total-limit and quasi-compact-open extension/total-limit comparisons, those finite proper/open maps give the completed-adjunction projection itself, with its actual units and counits. More precisely, for each coefficient ring $H=\mathcal O_E,\mathcal O_F$, its completion reflector $\widehat{(-)}$ with unit $\eta$ and proper direct image $P=Rp_{c*,H}$ satisfy, by [lem-pur-compact-support-completed-projection-coherence] applied to $u=p_c$ and the ideal $(\varpi_H)$,
$$\pi^c_{V,L}\eta_{PV\otimes^LL}=P(\eta_{V\otimes^Lp_c^*L})\pi^o_{V,L}$$
for complete $V,L$, where $\pi^o$ is the ordinary projection and $\pi^c$ the completed one. These identifications commute with the finite-free scalar mate, and the open factor has the same identification. The resulting equality is of integral morphisms; it does not assume that reduction functors are faithful.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] to the square with vertical arrows $p_c$ and horizontal identity-topos coefficient maps $A_n\to B_n$. The structural ring square commutes since all maps send a constant section to that same section. Its exchange is exactly $a_{p_c,n}$: both have transpose $C^{(n)}\varepsilon_{p_c,A_n}$ after the pullback/scalar comparison. The cited equality is thus the proper scalar/projection square. Apply the same statement on the ringed diagram sites of the quotient systems, using the proper mate supplied by [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate]. This proves an equality before evaluation. Also apply it to the constant integral square $A\to B$; denote that ordinary proper scalar mate by $a^o$. Neither application requires the coefficient square to be cartesian or the projection map to be invertible.

For the open factor use [lem-sf-open-tensor-normalization], including its ringed-diagram clause. On the extension-by-zero presheaf, both scalar/projection composites send $((x\otimes b)\otimes(y\otimes b'))$ to $(x\otimes y)\otimes bb'$ on every summand indexed by a map into the open, and send zero to zero on the remaining components. Tensor balancing and sheafification preserve this equality. The normalized open units identify these maps with the specified derived open maps. The formula also commutes with every quotient transition. Pasting this equality with Step 3 in the order $Rp_{c*}(b_j)\,a_{p_c}$ gives the compact-support projection square on the finite ringed diagram, for exactly $q_\bullet^c$ of [lem-pur-compact-support-strict-scalar-mate] and $\operatorname{PF}^c$ of [def-exchange-projection]. The same calculation gives the ordinary constant-integral square. Write its scalar comparison as $q^o=Rp_{c*,B}(b_j^o)a^o$.

proof.text: F6: properProjection_existsUnique follows directly from the completion-unit Hom bijection, without a separate completed-projection comparison. The principal Koszul reflector [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector], the unit-preserving principal-cone/quotient comparison [lem-pur-integral-principal-cone-quotient-comparison], the completeness equivalence [lem-pur-roos-intrinsic-completeness-equivalence], and the exact small-site transport [lem-pur-native-principal-completeness-small-model] show, on an arbitrary scheme, that quotient completion has complete output and precomposition by its actual unit is bijective into every complete object. Reuse the fully proved general reflectorFacts helper from OpenRoosUnitAdjunction; unlike that module's final geometric theorem this helper has no finite-type or field-of-definition hypotheses. Its adic datum is supplied by the valuation-ring DVR theorem [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]; an auxiliary prime different from ell supplies the Roos predicate's finite-field witness. Identify the actual inverse-image coefficient isomorphism with the normalized completed coefficient isomorphism by applying the sheaf adjunction Hom equivalence. This identifies push (completed l E) g with sfCompletedDerivedDirectImage. Reuse the proved completed_image_complete and complete_unrestricted helpers from SfCompleteDirectImageReduction, which transport the preservation-of-completeness assertion of [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison] to that actual derived functor. Hence the target push_g(C_Z(tensor(V,pull_g L))) is complete. Apply the unit Hom bijection to properProjectionOrdinary followed by push_g of the Z-completion unit. Surjectivity supplies the required map and equation; injectivity gives uniqueness. No faithfulness of finite evaluation, constructibility of the tensor, or invertibility of the ordinary projection is assumed. The additional identification with the whole finite quotient-diagram projection, needed by the still-open native and gamma comparisons, remains part of the original plan: apply [lem-pur-compact-support-completed-projection-coherence] to the principal uniformizer ideal and the actual direct-image adjunction, then transport by [lem-pur-completed-coefficient-pushforward-comparison], preserving counits and all tower transitions. proof.text: A4 (2026-10-27): openProjection_existsUnique follows directly from the completion-unit Hom bijection. Choose the principal DVR datum using the proved coefficient_datum helper of PrincipalKoszulStrictReplacement. Reuse the proved canonical dvrCoefficientModel_exists and dvrOpenModel_exists helpers of OpenQuotientKoszulCompleteness; these helpers require neither coefficient-prime invertibility on the scheme nor constructibility. The openDvrIntrinsicCriterion translates quotient completeness to intrinsic principal Koszul completeness. openDvrIntrinsicOpenTransport preserves the latter for a quasi-compact open immersion; the criterion then translates back. openDvr_ringed_identification transports this completeness to the actual completed-ring open extension. Completeness is invariant under this natural isomorphism. Completion of the inner tensor is complete on every scheme, hence its open extension is complete. The completion reflector Hom bijection extends the actual ordinary open projection followed by extension of the inner completion unit, and proves uniqueness. No new theorem hole is introduced. The following stronger finite-system comparison, needed by the remaining realization/native/gamma holes, remains the original plan: The compactification open is quasi-compact: for affine $V\subset\overline X$, $j^{-1}V=X\times_{\overline X}V$ is closed in $X\times_k V$ because $\overline X$ is separated over $k$; the latter is quasi-compact. Hence [lem-cbc-completed-extension-zero-comparison], applied to the identity base-change square, makes $j_!M$ complete and identifies it with the limit of its strict reductions. Apply [lem-pur-completed-open-tensor-system-realization] with $K=M$, $N=p_{c,H}^*L$ (completed pullback) for the open tensor factor. Its completion-unit equation identifies the completed open map with the finite system map and fixes its open unit. Together with Step 5 this identifies $P_H^c$ with $Rp_{c*,H}j_!$ and identifies the entire finite proper/open projection with the actual completed-adjunction projection. These comparisons are natural for morphisms of the input systems.

Precompose the two proposed maps with $\eta^F_{T_YZ}$. By the proper and open unit equations in Steps 5-6, scalar/unit compatibility in Step 8 and $\gamma=q^o$ from Step 7, their composites are the two ordinary scalar/projection paths of Step 4 followed by the target map induced by $T_XW\to\mathsf C_{F,X}T_XW$. Naturality of $q^o$ moves this last unit past its scalar mate; unit insertion identifies the completed pullback in $N$ with completion of the ordinary pullback. The ordinary paths are equal by Steps 3-4. The target is complete by Steps 5-6. Precomposition with $\eta^F_{T_YZ}$ is bijective on maps to a complete target by [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction], so the original integral composites agree. This also proves that the identifications commute with the finite-free scalar mate, while Step 4 gives the finite diagram assertion. No reduction functor has been assumed faithful.
